tagline: Clinical notes de-identified on the Mac before any AI sees them.
headline:
Premium AI for clinical letters.
The patient's identity stays on the Mac.
summary: Clinician's Veil finds the names, dates, addresses and references in a clinical note on the Mac itself, lets the clinician review every change, and only then lets one pseudonymised request go to a frontier model. The draft letter comes back, and the details are put back locally.

statement.label: Why I built it
statement.text: The best models write a good referral letter in seconds. But a clinical note is full of people, and identifiable patient information cannot simply be pasted into a chatbot.

points.title: The note
points.text: Names, dates of birth, addresses, references and the people around the patient.

points.title: The letter
points.text: GP letters, referrals and progress reports, written at the end of a long day.

points.title: The rule
points.text: Identifiable patient information does not leave without a justified purpose and approval.

points.title: The gap
points.text: Models small enough to run on a laptop find identifiers well, but do not write the letter as well as the best ones.

highlights.title: Found on the Mac, decided by the clinician
highlights.text: Rules and a BERT model find identifiers offline. Every proposal is accepted, kept or removed by hand, and anything missed is selected and added.
highlights.imageAlt: The review screen, with the original synthetic note beside the proposed result where the name, dates and address are placeholders.

highlights.title: Tokens out, one request at a time
highlights.text: The exact request is shown before it is sent. Every identifying detail is a one-off token, and each send needs its own approval.
highlights.imageAlt: The exact request payload, where the patient's details appear only as one-off tokens.

highlights.title: Names back, on the Mac
highlights.text: GPT-6 Sol drafts the letter, and the tokens are swapped back for the real details locally, ready to review and export as a PDF.
highlights.imageAlt: The draft referral letter with the synthetic patient's name and details restored on the Mac.

demo.title: A two-minute walkthrough
demo.summary: A synthetic referral note goes through local detection and review, then one approved request to GPT-6 Sol, and the letter comes back with the details restored on the Mac.

pages.title: How it works
pages.summary: From the note to the letter: what happens on the Mac, the one request that leaves it, and what never goes in that request.

pages.title: Architecture
pages.summary: A Tauri app with a plain Rust core, local models behind adapters, and one carefully built route out.
